title: FRESH AIR DISTRIBUTION - DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION
question: In what way do the Wemacs, CABIN AIR control cable, and CABIN HT control interact to adjust both the volume and temperature of fresh air supplied to the aircraft cabin?
answer: The amount of fresh air entering the cabin can be controlled by any of the six Wemacs. Rotating the Wemac valve will vary the airflow from fully closed to fully open.Airflow into the cabin can also be adjusted by the CABIN AIR control cable. Pulling the control fully aft allows the maximum amount of fresh air to flow through the distribution system. Pushing the control fully forward closes the scoop  and allows no fresh air to flow through the distribution system. NOTE:  Air temperature in the distribution system can be altered by use of the CABIN HT control. As the CABIN HT control is gradually pulled out, more and more heated air will blend with the fresh air from the scoop, and is distributed into the cabin. Either one or both of the controls may be set at any position from full open to full closed.

title: FRESH AIR DISTRIBUTION - DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION
question: How does the aircraft's fresh air system direct air from the fuselage side inlets into the cabin interior?
answer: Fresh air enters the cabin from one of three sources. Two of those sources are located on the leading edge of the wing  and the other source is located on the right and left sides of the fuselage, between the firewall and the forward door post. (1)  Fresh air from the leading edge inlets is distributed through a series of ducts to adjustable air outlet valves . Each wing feeds three Wemacs, with a total of six Wemacs located throughout the cabin. Wemacs are located at the upper corner of the windshield, between the instrument panel and forward doorpost, and overhead in the rear passenger area. (2)  Fresh air entering from the right side of the fuselage is controlled by an infinitely positionable scoop . This air is ducted directly into the heated air plenum and is distributed throughout the cabin.
